issue: Homepage shows large empty regions before the final CTA
reproduction_steps: Open the homepage and scroll past Why MinRosh. Two tall blank bands appear where news and feedback carousels should be, especially before JavaScript hydrates.
suspected_root_cause: Home carousels are client-only (ssr:false) and the loading placeholder reserves up to 1280px of empty surface.
recommended_correction: Render news and updates on the server, or use a short skeleton with real headings. Do not reserve a near-viewport blank block.
notes: Phase 6C: news renders in the initial HTML. The empty feedback carousel and its viewport-height placeholder are gone. Measured 0 ultra-snap placeholders on the isolated candidate. Before, port 3121 had 2 placeholders and no news heading at first paint.

issue: Mobile and tablet header consumes 167–226px
reproduction_steps: Load any public page. Measure the header box. At 320/390/430px it is about 225px; at 360px and 768px about 167px; at 1024px the primary nav overflows its container.
suspected_root_cause: Header chrome stacks the wordmark, descriptor, and controls, and the nav row overflows around 1024px (scrollWidth greater than clientWidth).
recommended_correction: Reduce mobile chrome toward one row plus menu. Stop nav overflow at 1024px and landscape tablet (1024x600). Keep touch targets at least 44px.
notes: Phase 2 measured header height and 1024 nav. Batch 1 rechecked service pages: header 140px static at 390, 103px fixed at 1440, no overflow.

issue: Hero heading is smaller on tablet than on a phone
reproduction_steps: Compare the homepage H1. At 390px it is about 36px. At 768px it is about 31px. At 430px it is about 39px.
suspected_root_cause: Hero size uses a viewport-width clamp whose middle range dips below the mobile floor.
recommended_correction: Use a scale that never shrinks the hero below the mobile size. Target roughly 36–40px mobile, 44–48px tablet, 56–60px desktop.
notes: Phase 3 measured homepage H1 scale. Not reopened in batch 1.

issue: Document titles are doubled with the site name
reproduction_steps: View the title tag. Many pages render as “Page | MinRosh Migration | MinRosh Migration”. 54 of 88 probed titles exceed 60 characters. News titles reach about 106 characters.
suspected_root_cause: Root metadata template appends “| MinRosh Migration” and page titles already include that suffix.
recommended_correction: Keep the suffix in one place only. Shorten news and destination titles so the brand appears once.
notes: Phase 6B: /newsletter/unsubscribe title is now "Unsubscribe | MinRosh Migration" with robots noindex, nofollow. buildMetadata strips a trailing brand suffix and keeps a brand-first title absolute so the root template cannot append the brand again. Upload document titles no longer include the suffix manually. Titles longer than 60 characters remain open. Phase 6D: homepage Open Graph and Twitter titles no longer add a second brand suffix. The document title stays one brand-first sentence. Phase 7B: the remaining defect was duplicated branding, not character length. A trailing "| MinRosh" plus the root template produced "| MinRosh | MinRosh Migration" on 21 titles. Titles that already contained "MinRosh Migration" before another clause, including About and the contact city string, also received a second suffix. buildMetadata now strips the short suffix and keeps a complete brand-bearing title absolute only when it already contains a clause separator. Contact is "Contact | Brisbane | MinRosh Migration". Education titles that said "visa alignment" or "permit alignment" now say study planning, DLI and study permits, or CAS and study planning. Page bodies were not rewritten. The isolated candidate build 8j6C9xBM3yqrH5Wtk4RSK on port 3125 has 0 doubled brand titles, 89 unique document titles, and 36 titles still over 60 characters. Those 36 are retained because the subclass numbers, destination names, study terms, and news topics are the search intent. Character length alone is not an open defect.

issue: Homepage repeats the same actions and explanations
reproduction_steps: Read the hero, the information-finder block, How MinRosh works, visa cards, tools, and the final band. Explore General Information and Education Course Enquiry appear as equal buttons many times.
suspected_root_cause: Homepage composes several sections that each restated the same two CTAs.
recommended_correction: Keep one primary and one secondary action in the hero. Later sections should add new information or a single quiet link.
notes: Phase 6C: the hero keeps one primary and one secondary action. The quiz and journey bands use a single text link. The closing band keeps one button and one text link. Identical action labels fell from 8 to 3 on first paint.

issue: Trust strip text is truncated
reproduction_steps: On a phone, the six trust items sit in a horizontal scroller. Supporting lines use very small type and line-clamp, so sentences are cut off.
suspected_root_cause: Bottom bar forces nowrap items with a 10px supporting size and line-clamp.
recommended_correction: Replace the six compressed items with three readable stacked items. Do not use type below 14px for public copy.
notes: Phase 3 measured the trust grid at 14px with no horizontal scroll. Not reopened in batch 1.

issue: 404 page drops the site header and uses a 16px heading
reproduction_steps: Open any unknown URL. The page is a lone card. There is no header, footer, or skip-target chrome. The real heading computes at 16px under a large pale 404 numeral.
suspected_root_cause: not-found.js renders a bare main and is not wrapped in SiteShell. The numeral is aria-hidden at 35% opacity.
recommended_correction: Render the 404 inside the public shell. Make “Page not found” the display heading. Keep the skyline decorative.
notes: Phase 6C: unknown URLs render inside the public header and footer. The H1 is 30px at 390 and 40px at 1440. Screenshot reports/visual-audit/screenshots/phase6c/390x844/this-route-should-404-6c.png.

viewport: all public pages with the footer
issue: Footer publishes internal operating counts
reproduction_steps: Every major page footer shows Enquiry count, Newsletter signups, and Updates tracked (observed values 3, 4, and 7; the count is sometimes blank before the stats request returns).
suspected_root_cause: SiteFooterInteractive renders /api/stats in the public footer.
recommended_correction: Remove operational counters from the public footer. They do not help a visitor and expose internal volumes.
notes: Phase 6C: the public footer no longer requests or prints enquiry, newsletter, or update counts. Confirmed across the 90-route crawl.

issue: Information Finder repeats its introduction and then leaves a large gap
reproduction_steps: The hero and the tool card repeat the same disclaimer. A tall empty area sits between the tool and the footer.
suspected_root_cause: Assessment page stacks a marketing hero and the same copy again inside the tool, with section spacing that does not collapse when content is short.
recommended_correction: Use one introduction. Tighten the gap before the footer.
notes: Phase 6C: the finder no longer repeats the hero disclaimer. The tool intro is one instruction line. Screenshot reports/visual-audit/screenshots/phase6c/1440x900/assessment.png.

issue: Booking page has an empty left column
reproduction_steps: Beside the form, a large pale panel has no illustration or meaningful content. The form itself is usable and consent boxes are unchecked.
suspected_root_cause: The session layout reserves a media column whose image or illustration is not rendering.
recommended_correction: Either show a real Brisbane image with alt text or remove the empty column so the form and explanation sit on one calm grid.
notes: Phase 3 booking page shows the Brisbane photograph and caption.

viewport: HTML source; all destination hubs and sections
issue: Destination HTML contains a second H1 from the loading shell
reproduction_steps: Fetch the raw HTML. It includes “Preparing destination guidance” plus the real hub H1 (44 sitemap URLs). After hydration the visible H1 is only the real title.
suspected_root_cause: app/destinations/loading.js renders an H1 inside the suspense fallback, which is present in the streamed document.
recommended_correction: Do not use an H1 in loading UI. Prefer a status text that does not compete with the page heading, and avoid a long blank or flash state.
notes: Phase 6B: destination, news, and upload loading shells are status regions with a paragraph title, not a second main#main-content or H1. Measured one visible H1 and one #main-content on destination and news routes. Playwright 163/163 passed on the isolated candidate.

issue: Several destination sections have short meta descriptions
reproduction_steps: UK about is about 52 characters. UK FAQ, Canada education, UK contact, and UK education are under about 75 characters.
suspected_root_cause: Those section metadata strings are shorter than a useful snippet.
recommended_correction: Write unique descriptions of roughly 120–160 characters for each thin section. Do not change compliance meaning.
notes: Phase 6C: destination section meta descriptions that were under about 110 characters now run from 120 characters upward. Official source names and the general-information limit are unchanged.

issue: Public pages exist outside the sitemap
reproduction_steps: /visa-services and /global-pathways return 200 and are not in sitemap.xml. /thank-you is noindex. /book-consultation 308s to /book-information-session.
suspected_root_cause: STATIC_SITEMAP_ROUTES omits those app routes.
recommended_correction: Decide which of those URLs should be indexed. Add the keepers to the sitemap and noindex or redirect the rest.
notes: Phase 6C candidate sitemap includes /visa-services and /global-pathways (85 URLs). Production was not updated.

issue: Education enquiry form dominates and crowds the supporting column
reproduction_steps: The form card is visually heavier than the official-source links beside it. The page still shows the required consent checkboxes unchecked.
suspected_root_cause: Premium form shell uses a large frosted card with equal visual weight to guidance.
recommended_correction: Keep the two-column structure. Reduce card padding and give the official-link column equal presence. Do not shorten consent text.
notes: Phase 6C: official study links sit beside the education form from the large breakpoint and stack above it on a phone. Consent text was not shortened.

issue: Pathway explorer repeats its disclaimer and then shows a plain link list
reproduction_steps: The hero disclaimer is repeated in the panel. Official links are unstyled text rather than the card system used on /tools.
suspected_root_cause: Explorer client renders a second disclaimer block and default anchors.
recommended_correction: Keep one disclaimer. Style links like the tools index. Do not imply eligibility scoring.
notes: Phase 6C: the explorer hero keeps the disclaimer once. Official links are bordered cards. Screenshot reports/visual-audit/screenshots/phase6c/1440x900/tools__pr-pathway-explorer.png.

issue: Cloudflare analytics beacon is blocked by Content Security Policy
reproduction_steps: Every reviewed page logs a console error: beacon.min.js violates script-src.
suspected_root_cause: CSP allows specific analytics hosts but not static.cloudflareinsights.com, while Cloudflare still injects the beacon.
relevant_file: next.config.mjs headers(); Cloudflare dashboard (do not change in this audit)
recommended_correction: Either allow that host in CSP or disable the Cloudflare web analytics injection. This is a console error, not a layout break.
notes: Phase 6D: the beacon is not in application code. Public CSP still omits static.cloudflareinsights.com and was not weakened. Disable the injection in the Cloudflare dashboard. The isolated candidate is not behind Cloudflare, so the console error was not retested there.

issue: Contact and other forms are calm, but the footer under them is dense
reproduction_steps: On a phone the enquiry steps work and checkboxes are not pre-ticked. The footer then stacks six link columns, stats, and a newsletter into a long block.
suspected_root_cause: Shared footer grid does not reduce column count or link spacing enough at 390px.
recommended_correction: Increase link spacing, group columns, and keep the legal notice readable. Do not remove disclosures.
notes: Phase 6C: phone footer is one column, links keep a 44px target, and the operational counts are gone. Disclosures remain.

issue: Navigation label casing is inconsistent
reproduction_steps: Header shows “POPULAR ROUTES” in capitals while other items are sentence case. The descriptor under the wordmark is much smaller than body text.
suspected_root_cause: GLOBAL_HEADER_PRIMARY_LINKS hard-codes the uppercase label.
recommended_correction: Use “Popular routes” and a 14px descriptor, or hide the descriptor under 1100px.
notes: Phase 6C: the header label is Popular routes. The pathway menu still opens from that item.

issue: News cards are even, but dates and tags feel like metadata rather than editorial hierarchy
reproduction_steps: Cards share one layout. Country tags and ISO-like dates compete with the headline.
suspected_root_cause: News index card component uses uniform chips.
recommended_correction: Lead with the headline, then a quieter date and source. Keep the official-source link.
notes: Phase 6C: news cards lead with the headline. Country and date sit underneath in smaller type. Screenshot reports/visual-audit/screenshots/phase6c/1440x900/immigration-news.png.

issue: 404 illustration is a generic skyline, not Brisbane
reproduction_steps: The card uses a mauve mountain silhouette at low contrast. It is marked decorative.
suspected_root_cause: SkylineSilhouette in not-found.js is an abstract path, not the Brisbane hero.
recommended_correction: If imagery is added, use the existing Brisbane river treatment. Do not add Sydney or stock travel imagery.
notes: Phase 6C: the 404 card uses the Brisbane river photograph instead of the generic silhouette.

issue: Regulatory wording was reviewed and should stay under human sign-off
reproduction_steps: Footer and heroes say MinRosh is not a registered migration agent and does not give immigration assistance. “Find a Registered Migration Agent” points at the public register, not a named partner. No public MARN, referral fee, or commission was found.
suspected_root_cause: Copy is the compliance disclosure, not a self-claim. A reviewer should confirm the register URL remains the official search page.
recommended_correction: Do not rewrite this copy to shorten the footer. Do not add partner names or MARNs.
notes: Compliance wording was not changed. Phase 6D reread the public claims and did not add a MARN, partner name, fee, or commission. /referral-program still describes tracked introducer links and needs a disclosure review. The personalised navigator and public AI chat stay off.

issue: Service pages leave a blank band between the header and the breadcrumbs
reproduction_steps: Open a core service page such as /employer-sponsored-visas. The header is in normal flow, and main still reserves about one header-height of empty space before the breadcrumb.
suspected_root_cause: portal-main--immersive padding-top uses the header height as if the header were fixed. Service pages do not load home.css, so the header stayed sticky, and at 768px it is static.
recommended_correction: Fix the premium header from 769px upward and drop the extra offset while the phone header is in normal flow.
notes: Phase 6B: premium headers stay fixed at every width and non-home main padding tracks the measured chrome height. Destination hubs that are not premium stay in normal flow on phones. /skilled-migration at 390 shows the breadcrumb directly under the header, with the heading fully visible.

issue: Contact and official-sources headings sit under the fixed header on phone and tablet
reproduction_steps: Open /contact at 390px. The header is position:fixed and 125px tall. The H1 top is 81px, so about 44px of the heading is covered. The same pattern appears on /australian-visas-official-sources (22px overlap at 390).
suspected_root_cause: Pages that import home.css keep the premium header fixed. The phone rule then sets main padding to 10px because it assumes the header is in normal flow.
recommended_correction: On viewports where the header is fixed, main padding must equal the measured header height. Do not apply the 10px in-flow padding to those pages.
notes: Phase 6B measured /contact and /australian-visas-official-sources at 320, 360, 390, 430, 768, 1024, 1440, and 1920, including 640px and 600px heights. Header is fixed. H1 top is below the header bottom at every size (contact gap about 71px at 390). Screenshots in reports/visual-audit/screenshots/phase6b/.

issue: Homepage mobile Lighthouse performance was 59 with a 4.7s LCP and 1210ms total blocking time
reproduction_steps: Lighthouse 12.8.2 mobile simulated throttling. The LCP element is the hero H1. About 90 percent of LCP was render delay while the body stayed at opacity 0 and the homepage loaded framer-motion.
suspected_root_cause: app/globals.css pageFade; components/ultra-maximum-layout.jsx always mounted effects
recommended_correction: Remove the opacity animation. Keep homepage sections on the server. Do not preload the decorative hero image ahead of the heading.
notes: Phase 6D isolated candidate on 127.0.0.1:3123, build k0tUGclUs32NqLfdiTybI. Mobile Lighthouse performance 95, LCP 2.7s, TBT 38ms, CLS 0.037. Accessibility, best practices, and SEO stayed 100, 100, and 92. Hero JPEG path and heading scale unchanged.

issue: Contact mobile Lighthouse recorded FCP but threw NO_LCP so the performance category was empty
reproduction_steps: The saved contact trace has FCP 1.7s and largest-contentful-paint error NO_LCP. The final URL is the contact page. The same body opacity animation delayed the first painted text.
suspected_root_cause: app/globals.css body fade
recommended_correction: Remove the body fade so the first HTML paint is visible without waiting for the main thread.
notes: Phase 6D contact mobile Lighthouse on 127.0.0.1:3123 records FCP 1.5s and LCP 3.2s. Performance 92, accessibility 100. The heading is 71px below the fixed header at 390px.
